findings.location: lib/promptRefinerShadowJournal.ts:487 (eventFrom, run_resumed `resumed.remainingCases <= 0`) with lib/promptRefinerShadowJournal.ts:665-669 (replay `resumable`) and lib/promptRefinerShadowJournal.ts:847-861 (resume branch appends run_resumed before any remaining-case guard)
findings.claim: A clean interruption after the 16th case terminal but before `run_completed` is reported resumable, yet resuming appends a `run_resumed` event with `remainingCases: 0` that the journal's own replay permanently rejects, so the run can neither complete nor be replayed afterwards — contradicting the documented contract that a clean post-terminal interruption resumes (docs/ops/prompt-refiner-shadow-harness.md section 5).
findings.reproduction:
In tests/promptRefinerShadowHarness.test.mjs style: `const done = journal("final-interruption"); runPromptRefinerShadowHarness({ corpus, journalPath: done, resume: false }); const full = texts(done); const j = full.journalText.trimEnd().split("
"); const w = full.witnessText.trimEnd().split("
"); const path = journal("final-interrupted"); const p = promptRefinerShadowPaths(path); writeFileSync(p.journal, j.slice(0, -1).join("
") + "
"); writeFileSync(p.witness, w.slice(0, -1).join("
") + "
");` (drops only the trailing `run_completed` entry and its witness line, i.e. a crash in that window). `replayPromptRefinerShadowJournal` on those two texts reports status `interrupted`, `unknownCases: 0`, `remainingCases: 0`, `resumable: true`. Then `runPromptRefinerShadowHarness({ corpus, journalPath: path, resume: true })` throws `prompt_refiner_shadow_resume_state` *after* writing the new entry, and every later `replayPromptRefinerShadowJournal` of the resulting files throws `prompt_refiner_shadow_resume_state` too. Expected: the resume completes the run, or is refused before any append leaves the journal unreplayable.

findings.location: lib/promptRefinerShadowJournal.ts:446 (eventFrom, run_stopped `stopped.remainingCases <= 0`) with lib/promptRefinerShadowJournal.ts:902-925 (mismatch stop appends before any remaining-case guard)
findings.claim: Same root cause on the stop path: a structural or behavioral mismatch on the last corpus case makes the harness write a `run_stopped` event with `remainingCases: 0` that its own replay rejects, so instead of the documented non-resumable `behavioral_fixture_mismatch`/`structural_boundary_violation` stop the operator gets `prompt_refiner_shadow_stop_state` and an unreplayable journal.
findings.reproduction: Copy the existing "a structural or behavioral mismatch stops non-resumably without a call" test but mutate the last case instead of the first: `const m = structuredClone(corpus); m.cases[15].expected = { status: "failed", failureCode: "invalid_response", refinedPrompt: null }; redigest(m); const v = validatePromptRefinerShadowCorpus(m); runPromptRefinerShadowHarness({ corpus: v, journalPath: journal("last-case-mismatch"), resume: false });` Actual: throws `prompt_refiner_shadow_stop_state`, and `replayPromptRefinerShadowJournal` on the written files throws the same. Expected: a report with `status: "stopped"`, `stopReason: "behavioral_fixture_mismatch"`, `resumable: false`, `processedCases: 16`.

findings.claim: The no-network trap only patches the CLI process (fetch/http/https/net/tls/dgram), not the `git` child process, so on a partial/blobless clone `git show <sha>:<path>` can lazily fetch objects from the promisor remote — network activity the trap cannot observe or block.
findings.reproduction: `git clone --filter=blob:none <remote> shallowish && cd shallowish && npm run shadow:prompt-refiner -- --journal=/tmp/j.jsonl --source-ref=<40-hex>` with the remote reachable; git fetches the allowlisted blobs over the network during the `git show` calls, while the same run under the test's trap reports no network use. A `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` / `--filter` guard or an explicit local-objects precondition would close it.

findings.claim: `Number(maxCasesText)` accepts non-decimal spellings, so `--max-cases=0x10` and `--max-cases=1e1` are silently taken as 16 and 10 rather than rejected as malformed input (the value is still bounded to 1..16 and safe-integer, so nothing unsafe follows).
findings.reproduction: `npm run shadow:prompt-refiner -- --journal=<new.jsonl> --source-ref=<40-hex> --max-cases=0x10` completes all 16 cases; expected an `argument_value_required`-style rejection from a `/^[1-9][0-9]*$/` check.

verdict.nextAction: Guard `remainingCases > 0` before appending `run_resumed`/`run_stopped` (and exclude `remainingCases === 0` from `resumable`, or let that state complete the run) so a final-case interruption or mismatch cannot write an event the replay rejects; re-run the 17 shadow tests with added last-case coverage.
